document.title: Task 2 · Working from home
document.text:
Working from home has become possible for many occupations that mainly involve digital information. This change offers employees greater flexibility, but it can also create difficulties for communication and wellbeing. I believe the advantages outweigh the disadvantages when employers provide clear support and retain opportunities for people to meet in person.

The most obvious benefit is the removal of a daily commute. Time previously spent travelling can be used for rest, family responsibilities or exercise, which may make working life more sustainable. Remote work can also expand access to employment. A qualified applicant who lives far from a major city may be able to accept a position without moving home. For employers, this creates a wider pool of potential staff. These advantages are particularly valuable when the work can be completed independently and its quality can be assessed through clear results.

There are nevertheless important drawbacks. New employees may find it harder to learn from experienced colleagues when everyday conversations take place online. Messages can be misunderstood, and arranging a formal meeting for every small question is inefficient. Some workers also struggle to separate work from private life, especially if they lack a quiet room or feel expected to answer messages at all hours. The flexibility of remote work can then become a source of pressure rather than a benefit.

These problems can be reduced through deliberate working arrangements. Employers should define reasonable contact hours, provide suitable equipment and organise regular opportunities for collaboration. A hybrid schedule may be especially useful for teams that need both focused individual work and shared discussion. In conclusion, remote work can save time and widen access to jobs, giving it considerable advantages. Its success depends on thoughtful management, however, rather than on the assumption that working outside an office automatically improves every employee’s life.
document.prompt:
WRITING TASK 2
Allow about 40 minutes.

More employees now work from home instead of travelling to an office. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Support your answer with reasons and relevant examples. Write at least 250 words.
PPB! original practice material.

annotations.quote: Working from home has become possible for many occupations that mainly involve digital information.
annotations.label: Position and scope
annotations.body: Answers the outweigh question explicitly and makes support a condition. A neutral list of pros and cons would not communicate this judgement.

annotations.quote: The most obvious benefit is the removal of a daily commute.
annotations.label: Developed argument
annotations.body: Connects saved commuting time to sustainable working life and remote hiring to access. Each benefit is explained, not merely named.

annotations.label: Counterpoint and response
annotations.body: Distinguishes collaboration costs from boundary problems at home. These disadvantages are credible and provide a basis for the solutions in the final paragraph.

annotations.quote: These problems can be reduced through deliberate working arrangements.
annotations.label: Synthesis
annotations.body: Defined contact hours and hybrid collaboration directly respond to the drawbacks. The conclusion restates why the benefits can outweigh them under these conditions.
